kernel.qtype: MQ4-G256 v2 (HFQ4-G256 layout, 136 bytes/group: 4B scale/zero header x2 + 128B packed nibbles)
kernel.op: y[row] += dot(A[row], x), residual add into y (read-modify-write)
kernel.weight_header_dtype: f16 scale,f16 zero (lane<16 reads u32@0, lane>=16 reads u32@4)
kernel.recipe_summary: four independent group streams per row (acc[g%4]); acc=(a0+a1)+(a2+a3); shfl_down 16,8,4,2,1 tree; two-row epilogue y.x=acc+y.x,y.y=bcc+y.y, odd last row y=y+acc; second-row DOG starts x1 then x0 (builder/SPIR-V); no atomics/LDS/scratch

arms.code_end_tail_fill: 0.4.3 regeneration of the shipped builder twin (builder 19fc7e2c): sha256 above are the regenerated objects, freeze_time_sha256 the 2026-10-11 freeze-time objects. The regeneration only appended the emitter's code-end tail fill (s_code_end words) to .text (4296 -> 4736 bytes; the freeze-time .text is a byte prefix). Kernel body, descriptors, symbols and metadata are unchanged; only the added tail, the ELF layout fields derived from the new .text size (section addresses/offsets, .relro_padding) and the _DYNAMIC symbol value in .symtab differ. No GPU hardware oracle, timing or Vulkan measurement was repeated and none is claimed (CPU compiler, static, emulator and RIP oracle checks run on the new objects are not hardware remeasurement); acceptance/oracle/timing/perf/receipt records and the 2026-10-11 pilot results stay bound to the freeze-time objects.

repeat_sequence.rule: Single process, per arm and per execution mode; the loaded executable handle is created once and reused across all three launches (no reload, no recompile between launches); kernarg rewritten per launch; fresh independent restored preimages every launch. Expected: launch 3 output frames byte-identical to launch 1 and to the cell's own arm result; launch 2 identical to its singleton. Catches stale pipeline/descriptor/specialization/kernarg/cache-state carry-over between K=6144 and K=17408.

limits: Pilot-owned files cited above are an uncommitted working tree at freeze: their sha256 pins identify the frozen bytes; consumers must refuse a different digest rather than follow the live file.

The registry snapshot (compile input of the pinned hipcc object) and kernels/src differ in text; this corpus binds the incumbent to the registry snapshot + object digest. Recipe equality between the two texts is not asserted here.
Arms V0, Hpm, Vpm do not exist; this document is not evidence of any parity.
Observed export (rev 2) is an export only: no lift/equality/replay proof exists, claims K1-K5 remain not_run.

The export was compiled by a PATCHED Mesa build (hook patch sha256 c258fbc9..., patched aco_interface.cpp/radv_shader.c etc.); the Mesa plan-source pins in `source_pins` are the unpatched files, and their line numbers may differ in the patched files. The V0 reference arm must be executed on the exact exported driver build (libvulkan_radeon.so sha256 65bd3163...).
The export disassembly used ROCm 10.1 llvm-mc (sha256 9ff7bd4c...), whereas Mesa pin.json names core-10.0; instruction text is advisory and is not the byte identity (shader.bin is).
Source pins stay the frozen snapshot; the pilot files are not re-pinned. The pilot's current file bytes were not re-hashed in rev 2.
